definition.body: The pharynx is a human-authored anatomical construct mapping the muscular tube that connects the posterior nasal apertures and oral cavity to the larynx and esophagus, serving both the respiratory and digestive pathways. Parameters: (1) the superior-to-inferior divisions — nasopharynx (behind the nasal cavity, above the soft palate), oropharynx (behind the oral cavity, between the soft palate and epiglottis), and laryngopharynx/hypopharynx (behind the larynx, from the epiglottis to the inferior border of the cricoid cartilage where it continues as the esophagus); (2) the muscular walls — three constrictor muscles (superior, middle, inferior) arranged in overlapping tiers plus longitudinal muscles (stylopharyngeus, salpingopharyngeus, palatopharyngeus) that elevate the pharynx and larynx during swallowing; (3) the compartments — the aerodigestive conduit that separates respiratory from digestive flow via the soft palate, epiglottis, and pharyngeal constrictor coordination; (4) the clinical landmarks — Waldeyer ring of lymphoid tissue (adenoids, palatine tonsils, lingual tonsil), the pharyngeal recess of Fossa of Rosenmüller, the esophageal opening. It persists as a maintained anatomical region in human anatomy texts, otolaryngology, and head-and-neck surgical atlases. e.g.: the pharynx as described in Gray's Anatomy, 42nd edition; nasopharyngeal carcinoma staging per the AJCC 8th edition using the pharyngeal recess; pharyngeal manometry measuring superior, middle, and inferior constrictor pressures | not: the esophagus (the digestive tube continuing from the pharynx at the cricoid level, distinct pathway); the trachea (the respiratory tube continuing from the larynx at the carina, distinct pathway); the oral cavity (the space anterior to the oropharynx, separated by the fauces) [formal: pharynx | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes]

payload.scope: People made the thyrohyoid membrane construct to map the fibrous sheet connecting the hyoid bone to the thyroid cartilage, so that clinicians can identify the superior boundary of the anterior laryngeal wall and navigate surgical approaches in the suprahyoid neck.

definition.body: The thyrohyoid membrane is a human-authored anatomical construct that maps the broad fibrous sheet extending between the superior border of the thyroid cartilage and the hyoid bone. Parameters: (1) the attachments — inferiorly attached to the superior border and superior horns of the thyroid cartilage, superiorly to the superior margin and tips of the greater horns of the hyoid bone; (2) the composition — a broad fibrous sheet with a thicker anterior margin and thinner posterior portions; (3) the relationships — anteriorly continuous with the infrahyoid musculature, posteriorly opens into a slit-like interval (the thyrohyoid hiatus) through which the internal laryngeal nerve and superior laryngeal vessels pass; (4) the lateral thickening — the lateral margins thicken into the thyrohyoid ligament, which provides the primary structural connection between the hyoid and thyroid cartilages; (5) the clinical access — a landmark for the thyrohyoid membrane puncture technique in percutaneous tracheostomy and a surgical approach window in anterior neck dissection. It persists as a standard anatomical structure in human anatomy texts, head and neck surgical atlases, and airway management guidelines. e.g.: the thyrohyoid membrane described in Gray's Anatomy, 42nd edition; the thyrohyoid membrane as a surgical landmark in anterior neck dissection per Cummings Otolaryngology, 6th edition; percutaneous tracheostomy via thyrohyoid membrane puncture in the journal of Critical Care Medicine [formal: membrana thyrohyoidea | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes]
